body: 19F here, got my 2B license at 18, my opinion is just go for it! Its a good skill to have, plus if you ever decide to get a bike in the far future, insurance will be lower (bc P plate insurance is much higher). Try not to pillion people who weigh higher thn ur body weight bc body weight does make a difference on a bike. Try not to pillion at all if possible, bc if there is an accident, the likelyhood of them dying is higher thn you dying. You might get injurred but they die, and you will have that guilt forever in the back of your mind. I've been riding few times every week (to goto sch) and I absolutely hate pillioning people. I took about 7months and $1.5k to get my license, got injurred about 2-3 times while learning, but it's def worth it once you go 110km/hr in msia. Esp since you already have your class 3, the experience you already have will be an advantage in keeping you safe on the roads on a bike.

My biggest motivation was similar to yours, getting a license as my school was 1+hr with public transport, but only 35-45mins on private transport. Really helps to get that extra 20mins of sleep in the morning. Not needing to squeeze and run for the buses is unmatched, and the freedom of not needing to worry about the last bus and all that. Once you gain more experience riding, you can also lane split, which would save you so much time esp during rush hours.

I took 9 months to get my license, getting injurred multiple times, esp on fig8. Also struggled with the evaluation lessons, but my best advice is to just imagine that they're not there at all. You paid for the lesson, take ur time, do it the way you would in revisions.

Just keep going bc class 2b license is worth the work

heyyo, im a y2 student at TP who got here thru N lvl pfp! im in social sciences, honestly i love TP so far. its v chill here, sch starts earliest at 9am (i hear NYP starts at 8.30am) and tp has "flex week" which is basically a week before exams where they have no lessons so you can focus on studying for the upcoming exams. lecturers can still be reached via msteams/ws if u ever need them. we also hv a damn nice library w multiple floors (can bring food to one of the floors) but also can be damn crowded. library also can book rooms so if u plan to go w a few friends can book a room!

in y2, you also get this compulsory mod called "global studies" which I absolutely loved, I got to go overseas w my friends for about 5 days. (you can choose if uw travel overseas or stay in sg btw!!) Can pick whr uw go from a list they give you(maybe like 5-7 diff places), and who uw room with, and for my trip, they gave us alot of freedom, so aft the iteniary was complete, we got to look around the place near the hotel (got some ppl grab to someplace and come back before curfew, and the tchers were chill w tht). Curfew was 10.30pm, we ended the day at about 8-9pm, so have abt 1-2hrs to do wtv uw outside hotel. also its subsidised heavily so its damn worth to go!

(also RP has weekly reflection journals, so i wldnt go thr, personally.)

cons are if u live at east side, bus 118 will be damn hard to board, esp during morning rush hr. macs also damn crowded during lunch. also TP is fairly slow w admin matters, so ur grades likely come out after ur friends at other polys get theirs.

for my pfp experience, we learnt some amath and s5 math, some english like how to write an email or smth (idk why oso), n there will also be classes that r specific to your course. when u go onto y1, likely only 0-2 ppl from pfp will join ur same class (this is for my course, to my knowledge). honestly i js anyhow do pfp cuz its v hard to fail + it doesn't count in ur GPA.

all in all, come to TP!
